questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Component Queries”?
options: Component Queries helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Component Queries means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Component Queries removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Component Queries should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Component Queries helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Component Queries is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “viewChild and viewChildren” in this lesson?
options: Treat “viewChild and viewChildren” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “viewChild and viewChildren” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “viewChild and viewChildren” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “viewChild and viewChildren” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “viewChild and viewChildren” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “viewChild and viewChildren” under Component Queries. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Component Queries”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
